title: Finance and cash
hired_for: An owner hires this screen to know what each order, product and channel really makes, to see a cash crunch weeks before it hits, and to never be surprised by taxes or money that did not arrive.

jobs.job: Tell me when cash will run low before it happens
jobs.why: A brand can be profitable on paper and still miss payroll because cash sits in stock or in payouts on the way. The owner needs weeks of warning, not days.

watch.metric: lowest expected bank balance in the next 13 weeks and the week it lands, refreshed weekly
watch.source: bank feed and accounting software (QuickBooks or Xero), open purchase orders, payroll and payout schedules

drives.metric: weeks of cash left above the owner's minimum cash floor

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: nobody can say when cash dips. After: the forecast shows a low of $38,000 in week 7, under the $50,000 floor, so a stock payment is split and the low rises to $61,000.
jobs.who_today: founder with a spreadsheet, or a fractional finance lead

jobs.job: Set how much I can spend on ads from total sales per ad dollar
jobs.why: Platform numbers claim credit for the same sale many times. Total store sales divided by total ad spend (marketing efficiency ratio) is the one number that cannot be double counted, and it sets a safe spend line.

watch.metric: marketing efficiency ratio: total store net sales divided by total ad spend, and the same for first orders only, weekly
watch.source: Shopify net sales and first-order flag, Meta and Google Ads spend

drives.metric: contribution margin after marketing per week

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: spend is set by platform return and the ratio fell from 4.1 to 3.2 in 6 weeks. After: a floor of 3.5 is set from margin and spend is trimmed to hold it within 2 weeks.

jobs.job: Know what I actually make on each order, product and channel
jobs.why: Revenue hides what is left after product cost, shipping, payment fees, discounts, returns and ads. Without this, the owner grows the channels and products that lose money.

watch.metric: contribution margin per order by channel and by product, after product, shipping, payment fees, discounts, returns and ad spend, weekly
watch.source: Shopify orders, landed cost in the brand brain, Meta and Google Ads spend, marketplace fee reports

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: the owner sees $420,000 in monthly sales and no margin split. After: Google Shopping shows $14 an order and TikTok shows minus $3, so $8,000 a month moves from TikTok to Google.
jobs.who_today: fractional finance lead, bookkeeper, or nobody

jobs.job: Stop promos that lose money before they go live
jobs.why: A sale, bundle or gift with purchase can need a sales lift the brand will never get. Checking the break-even before launch is cheaper than learning after.

watch.metric: sales lift needed to break even against the lift actually reached, per promo
watch.source: Shopify orders and discount codes, landed cost in the brand brain

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: last month's 30% off sale needed a 60% lift to break even and got 35%. After: the next promo is 15% off on 3 products and clears break-even before launch.

jobs.job: Know when each payout will land and chase the ones that did not
jobs.why: Money from Shopify Payments, PayPal, installment lenders and marketplaces arrives on different schedules, and some gets held or reversed. A late payout can break the cash plan.

watch.metric: payout dollars past their expected deposit date, by source, daily (for cash on delivery markets, courier remittances too)
watch.source: Shopify Payments payouts, PayPal, marketplace settlement reports, bank feed

drives.metric: cash in the bank against the cash forecast

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: $11,200 from 2 sources is 6 days past its expected date and nobody noticed. After: both are raised with the source the same day and land within a week.

jobs.job: Count every dollar we earn, not just the store's sales number
jobs.why: Sales on marketplaces, wholesale, TikTok Shop and retail often never reach the main report, and money owed but not yet collected goes unseen. The owner underrates channels and misses cash that is theirs.

watch.metric: share of total revenue that lands in one ledger with a channel tag, and revenue by channel including marketplaces and wholesale, monthly
watch.source: Shopify, marketplace settlement reports, wholesale invoices in accounting software

drives.metric: total revenue and total contribution margin across all channels

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: reports show $420,000 from the store and miss $95,000 from Amazon and wholesale. After: all 4 channels roll into one monthly number within 1 close.

jobs.job: Stay clear of sales tax trouble
jobs.why: Once sales into a state pass its limit (often $100,000 a year), the brand must register and collect tax. Missing it builds a debt plus penalties that the brand pays, not the customer.

watch.metric: count of states where trailing 12-month sales passed the tax limit with no registration on file, monthly
watch.source: Shopify tax reports or a tax tool (TaxJar, Avalara)

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: sales into 3 states passed the limit and only 1 is registered. After: the other 2 are registered and collecting within 30 days, stopping new debt.

jobs.job: Set prices from the profit I need
jobs.why: Prices set by feel or by a flat markup can sit below what the brand needs after shipping, fees and returns. A price set from a margin target protects every order.

watch.metric: contribution margin percent per product at the current price against the target, monthly
watch.source: Shopify orders, landed cost in the brand brain

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 9 products sit under the 30% margin target. After: 6 are repriced up $2 to $4 with no drop in orders, and 3 are bundled, within 45 days.

jobs.job: Cut products that lose money after all costs
jobs.why: Some products sell well and still lose money once shipping, returns and ads are counted. Growing them grows the loss.

watch.metric: count of products with negative contribution margin over 90 days, and their units sold
watch.source: Shopify orders, landed cost in the brand brain, ad spend by product

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 5 products lose $2 to $6 a unit and sold 3,000 units last quarter. After: 3 are repriced and 2 are cut, adding $9,000 a quarter.

jobs.job: Know the true landed cost of every product
jobs.why: If freight, duty and packaging are not counted per unit, every margin number above it is wrong.

watch.metric: share of products with a landed cost (product, freight, duty, packaging) updated in the last 90 days
watch.source: brand brain cost table, supplier and freight invoices in accounting software

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 40% of products still use last year's factory price with no freight or duty. After: all products carry a current landed cost and gross margin is restated 3 points lower.

jobs.job: Keep shipping cost from eating the margin
jobs.why: Free shipping thresholds, carrier rate rises and heavy parcels can quietly turn shipping into a large loss line.

watch.metric: net shipping cost (postage paid minus shipping charged) as a share of revenue, monthly
watch.source: Shopify orders and shipping labels or 3PL invoices

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: net shipping cost is 11% of revenue. After: the free shipping threshold moves from $50 to $65 and it falls to 7% within 30 days.

jobs.job: Count returns and refunds at their real cost
jobs.why: A refund costs the sale plus return postage, repacking and stock that cannot be resold. Leaving these out makes weak products look fine.

watch.metric: refunds, return postage and write-offs as a share of gross sales, monthly
watch.source: Shopify refunds and returns, 3PL invoices

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: returns cost 9% of gross sales but only refunds are counted. After: the full cost is on the report and the 2 worst products get a fix within 60 days.

jobs.job: Know how long new customers take to pay back what they cost
jobs.why: If a new customer takes 9 months to earn back their cost but stock money is tied up for 4, growth eats cash. The owner needs this before scaling spend.

watch.metric: months for each first-order cohort's gross profit to cover its acquisition cost, by monthly cohort
watch.source: Shopify orders by customer, Meta and Google Ads spend

drives.metric: safe spend on new customers per month

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: payback is unknown. After: it is 5 months for Meta customers and 11 for TikTok, so TikTok spend is held until its first order improves.

jobs.job: Split profit from new and returning customers
jobs.why: New customers often lose money on the first order and returning customers carry the profit. Mixed together, the owner cannot see whether acquisition pays.

watch.metric: contribution margin from first orders and from repeat orders as 2 lines, monthly
watch.source: Shopify orders with first-order flag, ad spend

drives.metric: acquisition budget set from first-order margin

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: one blended margin of 18%. After: first orders show minus 4% and repeat orders 38%, so the retention budget doubles and acquisition is capped.

jobs.job: Buy stock we can afford and will sell
jobs.why: A large purchase order paid early can empty the bank months before the stock sells. Every order should be checked against the cash forecast and a demand plan.

watch.metric: cash committed to open purchase orders against the forecast low point, per order
watch.source: purchase orders in the brand brain or accounting software, cash forecast

drives.metric: lowest expected bank balance in the next 13 weeks

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: a $120,000 order is due in 3 weeks and would push cash below the floor. After: it is split into 2 drops and cash stays above $50,000.

jobs.job: Free up cash stuck in slow stock
jobs.why: Stock that sits well past the supplier lead time is cash the brand cannot spend on growth, and it may need a markdown later.

watch.metric: days of stock on hand against supplier lead time per product, and dollars in stock older than 120 days, monthly
watch.source: Shopify inventory, landed cost in the brand brain

drives.metric: days from paying for stock to getting paid for it

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: $70,000 sits in 12 products with over 150 days of stock. After: a clearance plan turns $40,000 back into cash within 60 days.

jobs.job: Know when spending more on ads stops paying
jobs.why: Each extra ad dollar usually brings less than the one before. The owner wants to know where the next $10,000 goes further, or whether it should be spent at all.

watch.metric: new customer revenue gained per extra $1,000 of ad spend at current levels, trailing 28 days
watch.source: Shopify first-order revenue, Meta and Google Ads daily spend

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: the last $10,000 a week brought $14,000 in first-order sales, below break-even. After: that spend is cut back and weekly margin rises $2,500.

jobs.job: Set a safe ad budget for peak season
jobs.why: Black Friday to Christmas brings the most sales and the most risk. Spend, stock and cash need to be planned together weeks ahead.

watch.metric: planned peak season ad spend against the most the cash forecast and margin allow, set 8 weeks before peak
watch.source: cash forecast, Shopify history, ad spend plan

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: the agency plans $250,000 for November with no cash check. After: the plan is capped at $190,000 with a total sales to ad spend floor of 3.0.

jobs.job: Make sure the store, the payment processor and the books agree
jobs.why: If Shopify, the processor and the books show different sales, every decision and every tax filing rests on a guess.

watch.metric: gap between Shopify net sales, processor deposits and booked revenue, by named cause, monthly
watch.source: Shopify, Shopify Payments or processor reports, accounting software

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: the books and Shopify differ by 4% with no reason given. After: 3 causes are named (refund timing, gift cards, fees) and the unexplained gap is under 1%.

jobs.job: Keep payment fees in check
jobs.why: Card, wallet and buy now pay later fees differ a lot by method. As the mix shifts, fees can quietly take another point of margin.

watch.metric: payment fees as a share of sales, by payment method, monthly
watch.source: Shopify Payments, PayPal and installment lender reports

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: fees rose from 2.9% to 3.6% of sales as installment use grew. After: installments show only above $75 and fees return to 3.1%.

jobs.job: Forecast next month's sales, new and returning
jobs.why: Stock orders, ad budgets and hiring all depend on the sales forecast. One blended guess misses when new customer growth stalls.

watch.metric: forecast against actual revenue, split new and returning customers, monthly
watch.source: Shopify orders, marketing calendar in the brand brain

drives.metric: stock and spend decisions made on the forecast

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: forecasts miss by 20% most months. After: new and returning sales are forecast separately and the miss falls to under 8% within 3 months.

jobs.job: Keep overheads to the plan
jobs.why: Software, contractors and office costs creep up one small bill at a time. Without a monthly check against the budget, profit leaks.

watch.metric: operating spend against budget by category, monthly
watch.source: accounting software and card feed, budget in the brand brain

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: software and contractors run 22% over budget. After: 6 unused tools and 1 contractor are cut and spend is back within 5% next month.

jobs.job: Compare financing offers against my real cash forecast
jobs.why: Revenue-based loans and inventory financing can look cheap and cost a lot once fees and repayment timing are counted. The owner needs the true cost and the cash effect side by side.

watch.metric: total yearly cost of each offer and the lowest cash week once repayments are added
watch.source: lender term sheets and the cash forecast

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: a lender offers $150,000 for a 6% fee that is really 28% a year. After: the owner compares 3 offers and picks one that keeps cash above the floor at 14% a year.

jobs.job: Treat gift cards and store credit as money we owe
jobs.why: Unused gift cards and store credit are promises to ship product later. Counting them as sales overstates profit.

watch.metric: outstanding gift card and store credit balance, monthly
watch.source: Shopify gift card and store credit reports

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: $32,000 in gift cards sold at the holidays was booked as sales. After: it is held as owed and moves to revenue only as cards are used.

jobs.job: Close the books fast each month
jobs.why: When the month takes 3 weeks to close, the owner decides on numbers that are a month old.

watch.metric: days from month end to closed books
watch.source: accounting software close date

drives.metric: age of the numbers used for decisions

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: books close 21 days after month end. After: payouts and bills are matched weekly and the close takes 7 days.
